title: Day 588 Mañanera (Martes de Seguridad): Homicides Down 40% Since Oct 2024 Inauguration; 800+ Guerrero Families Displaced by Los Ardillos Drone Attacks; EU-Mexico Summit Confirmed for May 22
detail: On May 12, 2026 (Day 588), President Claudia Sheinbaum held her Security Tuesday mañanera (Martes de Seguridad) from the Salon de la Tesorería at the National Palace, with Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch presenting the full crime incidence report through April 2026. Five major developments: (1) SECURITY STATISTICS: García Harfuch announced that intentional homicides have fallen 40% in daily average since Sheinbaum took office on October 1, 2024 — from 86.9 homicides per day during the final full year of the AMLO administration to 52.5 per day as of April 2026. Sheinbaum framed this as a historic 19-month decline, the lowest daily average since 2015. (2) GUERRERO DISPLACEMENT CRISIS: García Harfuch specifically named two criminal groups — Los Ardillos and Los Tlacos — as the primary drivers of a forced displacement emergency in Guerrero's Montaña Baja region. More than 800 families have been forced to flee their homes in Chilapa de Álvarez municipality following drone and firearms attacks by Los Ardillos on indigenous communities in the towns of Tula, Xicotlan, Acahuehuetlan, and Alcozacan. Separately, four members of the indigenous self-defense organization CIPOG-EZ (Coordinadora de Pueblos Indígenas) have been reported disappeared after the attacks. Sheinbaum pledged federal coordination with SEGOB and the security cabinet to ensure displaced families could return safely. (3) EU-MEXICO SUMMIT CONFIRMED: Foreign Affairs Secretary Roberto Velasco confirmed that EU Council President António Costa and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will arrive in Mexico City on May 21, with the formal EU-Mexico Summit scheduled for May 22, 2026. The summit will formally sign the modernized EU-Mexico Global Agreement — an event of major diplomatic and economic significance. All 27 EU member states had approved the agreement on May 11. The deal is projected to increase EU-Mexico bilateral trade by 35% over five years, covering agri-food, automotive, manufacturing, and pharmaceutical sectors. (4) SCHOOL CALENDAR / SEP: SEP confirmed that summer vacations will NOT be advanced. Sheinbaum noted the earlier agreement to push vacations to June 5 due to heat waves and the 2026 World Cup was a unanimous decision by all 32 state education secretaries plus Mexico City — consistent with her defense of Education Secretary Mario Delgado the previous day. (5) DRUG POLICY FRAMING: Legal Counsel Luisa María Alcalde cited Trump's own 2026 National Drug Control Strategy document — which explicitly acknowledges the United States has a severe domestic drug consumption and public health problem — as diplomatic ammunition to reinforce Mexico's longstanding demand that drug policy be treated as a bilateral public health issue rather than a unilateral U.S. security imposition. The move was part of a coordinated messaging strategy ahead of the USMCA first formal negotiating round (on track for the week of May 25). BACKDROP: The Trump administration's review of all 53 Mexican consulates in the U.S. continues; the CIA-Chihuahua FGR probe is ongoing; the DOJ indictment of suspended Sinaloa Governor Rocha Moya (on 30-day leave since May 2) remains unresolved; Banxico's rate cycle has ended at 6.50%.

media.caption: Sheinbaum's May 12 Security Tuesday mañanera: 40% homicide decline, Guerrero displacement crisis addressed, EU-Mexico Summit confirmed for May 22
